notes: EVENT: Intel ISEF 2018, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA (host city confirmed by the Wikipedia ISEF article mirror on GitHub: 'ISEF 2018 (Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania)'). From memory and NOT re-verified in this session: held May 13-18, 2018 at the David L. Lawrence Convention Center, awards ceremony Friday May 18; Society press materials said approximately 1,800 finalists from 81 countries, regions and territories, ~US$5 million in awards. Observed in the local master CSV (export of the Society for Science abstracts database): 1,390 project rows for 2018 (projects, not finalists -- team projects are one row) from 82 distinct 'Fair Country' values, which include territories/regions (Guam, Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Northern Mariana Islands, US Virgin Islands, Hong Kong SAR, Macao SAR, Chinese Taipei, Northern Ireland, Palestine). METHOD/LIMITS: the session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this task started, and the egress proxy blocks societyforscience.org, abstracts.societyforscience.org, sspcdn.blob.core.windows.net, wikipedia.org, web.archive.org and news sites; only github.com/raw.githubusercontent.com were reachable. Every record therefore comes from (a) /home/user/Radon-and-Bradyseism-model/isef_research/data/isef_master_2017_2026.csv, whose ProjectId column maps to https://abstracts.societyforscience.org/Home/FullAbstract?ProjectId=N and whose 'Awards Won' field reproduces the official award strings (e.g. 'Intel ISEF Best of Category Award of $5,000', 'First Award of $5,000', 'Gordon E. Moore Award', 'Intel Foundation Young Scientist Award', 'Dudley R. Herschbach SIYSS Award', 'European Union Contest for Young Scientists Award'), and (b) the GitHub mirror of the Wikipedia ISEF article (top-award names with hometowns). The official Society press releases ('Intel ISEF 2018 Grand Awards' / 'Special Awards', May 18 2018, cited by Wikipedia as 'Intel ISEF 2018', Society for Science & the Public, May 18, 2018) could not be fetched. TOP AWARDS: Gordon E. Moore Award US$75,000 -> Oliver Nicholls (Barker College, Sydney, Australia; Robotics and Intelligent Machines; also Best of Category + First Award + INCOSE honorable mention, IEEE Foundation 2nd $600, NASA 2nd $750). Two Intel Foundation Young Scientist Awards US$50,000 each -> Meghana Bollimpalli (Little Rock Central High School, Little Rock, AR; Chemistry; also Best of Category + First Award + ACS honorable mention) and Dhruvik Parikh (Henry M. Jackson High School, Bothell, WA; Energy: Chemical). Wikipedia mirror and CSV agree on all three names. Prize amounts ($75,000 / $50,000) are the standard 2018 amounts given in the task brief; the CSV award strings carry no dollar figure for these two awards. No Craig R. Barrett (2019+), Horvitz (2021+), Peggy Scripps (2022+), Yancopoulos (2023+) or Mary Sue Coleman awards existed in 2018. GRAND AWARD AMOUNTS 2018 (from the award strings): First $5,000, Second $2,000, Third $1,000, Fourth $500 (raised from 2017's $3,000/$1,500/$1,000/$500); Best of Category $5,000. CSV counts: 35 First, 68 Second, 102 Third, 136 Fourth, 166 special-awards-only, 882 no award. Every Best of Category winner also holds a First Award of $5,000 in the same category. BEST OF CATEGORY: 20 of the 22 categories are documented by an explicit 'Intel ISEF Best of Category Award of $5,000' string. The 21st entry, Energy: Chemical -> Dhruvik Parikh, is INFERRED, not read from a source: his CSV award string shows only 'Intel Foundation Young Scientist Award', but the Society selects the Moore and Young Scientist awards from among the Best of Category winners, and the export is systematically incomplete for exactly this category -- none of the 41 Energy: Chemical rows and none of the 58 Materials Science rows carries ANY grand-award string (First-Fourth), whereas every other category shows 1-2 First awards and 2-5 Second awards. Treat the Parikh BoC entry as highly probable but unverified. NOT FOUND: Materials Science Best of Category 2018 (and all Materials Science / Energy: Chemical First-Fourth grand awards). Daniel Kang (John F. Kennedy High School, Guam; Materials Science; 'Novel Graphene Nanoplatelet Embedded Pigmentless Emulsions for Low Cost Paintable Capacitive Sensors and Supercapacitors') won the EUCYS trip award, which usually goes to top-placing finalists, so he is a plausible candidate for the Materials Science BoC, but this is NOT asserted. SIYSS / EUCYS: two Dudley R. Herschbach SIYSS Award winners found -- Nabeel Quryshi (Biomedical and Health Sciences BoC) and Muhammad Abdulla (Mathematics BoC); the Society normally names 2-3 per year, so a third winner from the two gap categories cannot be excluded. Two European Union Contest for Young Scientists Award winners found -- Rhea Malhotra (Biochemistry BoC) and Daniel Kang (Materials Science). EUCYS 2018 took place in Dublin, Ireland (Sept 2018) -- from memory. OTHER NOTABLE FIRST AWARDS 2018: Krithik Ramesh (Cherry Creek HS, CO; Engineering Mechanics) who went on to win the 2019 Gordon E. Moore Award; Erin Smith (FacePrint, Behavioral and Social Sciences); Syamantak Payra (Robotics); Lillian Petersen (Earth and Environmental Sciences, food-shortage prediction from satellite imagery); Hwa Chong Institution team (Singapore, Chemistry); Aaron Hannon (Ireland, Embedded Systems). FIELD CONVENTIONS: 'names' are 'Last, First' as in the Society database, team members separated by '; '. 'school' comes from the database; 'location' gives the affiliated-fair state/country (the database does not carry home city) except for the three top winners whose hometown comes from the Wikipedia mirror. Minor normalisations: 'Lim , Bryan' -> 'Lim, Bryan', trailing spaces trimmed ('Wilson, Amanda', 'Tomov, Sofia'); 'Friedensschule Munster' kept without umlaut as in source. first_awards = all 35 First Award rows in the CSV (including the 20 explicit BoC winners); second_awards = all 68 Second Award rows. DISAGREEMENTS: none found between the two sources used. CATEGORIES 2018 (22): Animal Sciences; Behavioral and Social Sciences; Biochemistry; Biomedical and Health Sciences; Biomedical Engineering; Cellular and Molecular Biology; Chemistry; Computational Biology and Bioinformatics; Earth and Environmental Sciences; Embedded Systems; Energy: Chemical; Energy: Physical; Engineering Mechanics; Environmental Engineering; Materials Science; Mathematics; Microbiology; Physics and Astronomy; Plant Sciences; Robotics and Intelligent Machines; Systems Software; Translational Medical Science (no Technology Enhances the Arts yet).
